Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-11

Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE); Jordan Liu (Redwood SE); Priya Desai (Redwood CSM); Maria Gonzalez (Nexera - Procurement); Omar Patel (Nexera - Security); Lisa Chen (Nexera - GC); Tariq Ahmed (Nexera - Platform)

--- Transcript body (timestamps approximate) ---
[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we have about 45 minutes, quick intros?
[00:10] Maria Gonzalez: Hi Maria here, I'll be managing procurement and the legal loop, bringing Lisa and Omar in for security and compliance.
[00:15] Lisa Chen: Hi, Lisa. We'll focus on MSA/DPA exceptions and audit cadence.
[00:20] Alex Kim: Great, Jordan from our side is the technical lead for any benchmark or private deployment questions. Jordan, quick intro?
[00:26] Jordan Liu: Hey all, Jordan Liu, platform SE, I own the deployment and perf story, happy to deep dive into KV cache, batching, quantization tradeoffs.
[00:34] Tariq Ahmed: Tariq here - we'll want to understand network topology, egress, and how KMS integrates with our on-prem HSM.
[00:42] Alex Kim: Perfect. Agenda for today: 1) procurement timeline and approvers, 2) contract redlines (MSA/DPA/SLA), 3) technical gating items for private/hosted options, and 4) next steps.
[00:55] Maria Gonzalez: Timeline: procurement needs final MSA signed by Jan 12 to hit our Q1 rollout. Primary approvers are me, then Lisa and FinOps. We rarely accept open-ended data retention terms.
[01:06] Lisa Chen: Yep, we need specifics on retention, deletion APIs, and ability to audit. Also SOC2 report frequency and right to audit clauses.
[01:16] Omar Patel: Security questions: do you offer customer-managed keys? Is there a VPC/private plane option? Any FedRAMP-like artifacts?
[01:25] Jordan Liu: Quick answer: for keys Redwood offers KMS integration options - hosted KMS with envelope encryption or customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS/Azure Key Vault, and for private we can support VPC peering or an on-prem package. There may be some limited feature differences between hosted and private.
[01:40] Omar Patel: When you say limited differences, can you be concrete? For example, can KV cache be used in private deployment with our HSM?
[01:50] Jordan Liu: The KV cache is a runtime-level optimization, it doesn't store raw inputs persistently. In our private package we can configure local cache storage behind your network. Regarding HSM, we integrate with customer KMS via standard APIs; there are config steps but it's supported - might require our infra team for the initial setup.
[02:10] Tariq Ahmed: So initial setup means our infra will open some ports and we run a bootstrap? How long does that usually take?
[02:18] Jordan Liu: Typically 2-4 weeks for the first customer on-prem integration; if you go VPC with our private plane it's faster, often under 10 business days if your network team is responsive.
[02:28] Maria Gonzalez: That timeline is helpful. Can we discuss the SLA? We need 99.9 availability and monthly credit allowances in the MSA.
[02:38] Alex Kim: Redwood Dedicated offers SLA-backed uptime. Our standard MSA includes service credits tied to outages; we can propose language to align with 99.9, but there are tiers depending on committed capacity.
[02:48] Lisa Chen: Also we'd like to see audit logs for individual API calls, not just aggregated metrics.
[02:55] Jordan Liu: We surface per-request tracing in the Console; for Private deployments we can ship syslog-forwarding or S3-compatible log sinks. The Console is more opinionated for hosted.
[03:10] (audio glitch)
[03:20] Maria Gonzalez: On pricing — procurement will want reserved capacity pricing and an estimate of token cost and peak throughput. We need an example commitment contract.
[03:31] Alex Kim: We can provide reserved commits with lower unit rates; I'll send a sample pricing schedule. For benchmarking, Jordan can simulate your expected mix (chat vs long-form generation) and show token economics at scale.
[03:45] Omar Patel: One of our concerns is PHI. If PHI is in prompts, can Redwood guarantee it won't be used to train models?
[03:54] Priya Desai: Priya (CSM) here — we have a data usage line in the DPA; hosted enterprise customers can opt-out of any training usage and we can offer Private where no data leaves your VPC. We'll include explicit no-training language in the DPA redline.
[04:10] Lisa Chen: Ok we need that in writing. Also retention windows and deletion APIs.
[04:18] Alex Kim: Understood, we'll mark those redlines.
[04:22] Tariq Ahmed: For the network side, what ports and egress are expected if we do VPC peering? Any egress fees?
[04:31] Jordan Liu: For VPC peering, it's standard TLS over 443; egress fees depend on cloud region and provider, we'll provide an estimate. If on-prem, we do a site-to-site setup.
[04:45] Maria Gonzalez: Another legal item: indemnity and limits of liability. Our legal team wants tighter caps for PHI breaches. Is there room for negotiation?
[04:55] Alex Kim: We can discuss caps; we have templates that escalate caps based on enterprise plans and committed spend. I'll flag legal to prepare a proposal.
[05:05] (brief cross talk)
[05:12] Omar Patel: Can you share SOC2 and penetration test artifacts under NDA?
[05:18] Priya Desai: Yes, we can share SOC2 Type II summary and pen test reports after an NDA. We'll send the attestation pack.
[05:28] Lisa Chen: Great. Also related to SLA, do you offer automatic fallbacks to smaller models if capacity is constrained? Need to make sure we don't have sudden latency spikes in prod.
[05:38] Jordan Liu: Yes, Redwood Smart Routing can fallback to compatible model variants; that's configured per-route in the Console with canary rules. We'll show a sample fallback policy in the runbook.
[05:50] Maria Gonzalez: For procurement, we need a clean redline of the MSA and DPA and a short one-pager describing what the private option entails and the differences vs hosted.
[06:02] Alex Kim: We'll provide a redline summary and a plain-English one pager.
[06:08] Tariq Ahmed: For the benchmark, we want to run 2 scenarios: 1) Live chat (500-1k token turns, high qps), 2) Document summarization (3k tokens). Can you simulate with your Dedicated nodes?
[06:20] Jordan Liu: Yes, we can spin up a dedicated pool for a short non-prod window; we'll need sample traffic patterns and prompts to match. Expect a short cost estimate for the run.
[06:32] Maria Gonzalez: Good. Timeline wise, if we get redlines by Dec 16 and internal approvers by Dec 18, do you think legal can get us to MSA signature by Jan 12?
[06:44] Lisa Chen: That depends on how many redlines we have, but it's feasible with dedicated back-and-forth.
[06:50] Alex Kim: We'll prioritize the redline packet for you.
[06:55] (15 min of more detailed discussion about specific contract clauses - content summarized)
[07:10] Lisa Chen: Clause 4.2 around data processing — we'd like to stipulate 30 day maximum log retention unless otherwise needed for investigation. Can you support that?
[07:22] Jordan Liu: For hosted customers, standard retention is 90 days for traces but audit logs can be configured. For enterprise customers we can map retention to your policy; if you need 30 days we can propose that in the DPA.
[07:34] Omar Patel: On encryption in transit and at rest — do you use customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest in hosted?
[07:41] Jordan Liu: Hosted default uses Redwood-managed KMS, but enterprise hosted customers can bring your own KMS keys (BYOK) via AWS KMS or similar. Private deployments always use customer-managed keys in your control.
[07:54] Maria Gonzalez: Any regulatory artifacts for HIPAA specifically?
[07:58] Priya Desai: We don't advertise HIPAA certification, but we have customers using Redwood with PHI under a BAA and specific configuration - it's something we can discuss and document.
[08:10] Maria Gonzalez: Ok we'll need a BAA draft.
[08:15] Alex Kim: We'll add that as an ask.
[08:18] (audio - short dropout)
[08:28] Tariq Ahmed: Quick question - live config changes and rollout. How do canary deploys work for model updates?
[08:36] Jordan Liu: Canary deploys are done at the routing layer; you can do % traffic rollouts and automatic rollback on error thresholds. We include tracing so you can correlate latency/regressions to prompt sets.
[08:50] Lisa Chen: For compliance, we need immutable logs and tamper evidence. Is that supported?
[08:57] Jordan Liu: We can stream logs to your S3 with object versioning or to Splunk via forwarders; tamper-proofing requires your storage policy but we can enable write-once storage patterns.
[09:10] Maria Gonzalez: Ok I think we're clear on tech gating. On pricing: can you give a ballpark committed minimum for dedicated to reach our target of 50 qps?
[09:22] Alex Kim: I'll put together a model. Off the cuff, XXk per month for the committed pool but I'll send a detailed schedule.
[09:30] Lisa Chen: Please include the cost delta for BYOK and private deployment.
[09:34] Alex Kim: Will do.
[09:37] (closing 5 minutes recap)
[09:40] Alex Kim: Recap: Redwood will send MSA/DPA redline summary, SOC2 and pen test under NDA, BYOK/KMS integration notes, pricing schedule and a one-pager on private vs hosted. Jordan will prepare benchmark plan and runbook. Nexera will confirm approvers and target dates. Any final items?
[09:57] Maria Gonzalez: No, that covers it. Thanks.
[10:02] Lisa Chen: Thanks everyone.
[10:05] Alex Kim: Thanks, we'll follow up with the packet by Dec 16.
